step1_skipMechanism.countingRule: READ-ONLY, live, against production (PRODUCTION_NEONDB_URL via gcloud secret, cad_property + place_layer_snapshots; PRODUCTION_HAUSKA_MCP_URL via gcloud secret, atoms) for county 48055 (Caldwell). No writes anywhere.
step1_skipMechanism.dispatchDiagnosisAsStated: "the bake reads the current vintage, gets no CAD claim for these accounts, and skips them entirely" -- this is CLOSE but not the literal mechanism. It correctly names the symptom class (roll-absent accounts) but not the code path that actually causes today's observed skip.
step1_skipMechanism.actualMechanismFound: nodeFacetBakeTier1ConformantCli.ts selects EVERY conformant-v1 cad-parcel-roll atom for the county with no vintage filter (conformantCadCountyWhere has none). For each it derives situs via situsForBake(body), which calls assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly on the ATOM'S OWN claim.situsAddress (serveGuards.ts: PUNCTUATION_ONLY_RE = /^[\s,.\-;:'"`]+$/). Exactly 63 of Caldwell's atoms carry claim.situsAddress === ', ,' (a bare punctuation placeholder). assertSitusNotPunctuationOnly throws SITUS_PUNCTUATION_ONLY; situsForBake catches it and returns {situs:null, refuse:true}; the CLI's per-row loop does `if (refuseSitus) { skippedBadSitus += 1; continue; }` BEFORE the write -- the row is never touched. It is not a 'no CAD claim found' branch (no such branch exists in the code today); it is the pre-existing situs-quality guard firing on stale claim content.
whyThisIsTheRightDiagnosis: cad_property tax_year 2025=24,989 rows, tax_year 2026=48,382 rows, both counts reconfirmed live and matching the dispatch exactly.
prop_ids present at tax_year 2025 and ABSENT at tax_year 2026 (EXCEPT query): 267, not 63.

Of those 267, exactly 63 have situs_address that is punctuation-only per PUNCTUATION_ONLY_RE -- an EXACT match to the dispatch's '63' count. The other 204 have normal-looking situs (real streets, real legal descriptions, real market values in the STALE 2025 cad_property row).

place_layer_snapshots for adapter node-facets:tier1, county 48055: schema distribution is {node-facets-tier1-conformant-v1: 48586, node-facets-tier1-v1 (OLD shape): 63}. The 63-on-old-shape set is the SAME 63 punctuation-only prop_ids (spot-checked 48055:1, exact match). None of them were touched by last night's Caldwell bake run (all 48,649 Caldwell tier1 snapshots show updated_at before 2026-09-09T00:00Z; the freshest is 2026-09-08T20:16:34Z for live parcels).

The 204 non-punctuation roll-dropouts are NOT stuck -- they DO get rebaked every run (bakedAt 2026-09-08T20:09:30Z, same run as everything else), reading conformant-v1, using their own atom's stale 2025 claim for baseFacts and correctly reading null/absent for the dollar-roll fields (those come from fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll pinned to the declared 2026 vintage, which has no row for a departed prop_id, so cadRoll.marketValue etc. bake honest-null there already -- that specific sub-field is not broken).
step1_skipMechanism.scopeCorrection: The dispatch's '63 stale parcels' undercounts the true defect population for Caldwell by roughly 4x. 267 prop_ids are absent from the current (2026) roll. All 267 share the SAME underlying defect the operator ruled on -- an account absent from the current roll is being served as though current, with nothing saying so -- but only the 63 punctuation-only ones are VISIBLE today (stuck on the old schema, failing the walk). The other 204 are a QUIETER version of the identical defect: they get a fresh bakedAt every run and read as normal, current conformant-v1 rows, using a departed account's year-old situs/acreage/legal-description content with no absence marker anywhere. This is the DEV_PROCESS 1.4 case (two numbers that should agree and do not): 'accounts absent from the current roll' (267) and 'accounts the walk currently flags' (63) are not the same number and must not be reported as one. Recommendation carried into implementation: gate the retirement declaration on ROLL ABSENCE (prop_id not present in fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll's declared-vintage map, which the bake already fetches every run) rather than on the situs-punctuation symptom, so the fix covers all 267, not only the 63 the walk happens to catch today. Flagging this to the operator/integration seat as an open question on final scope, since the dispatch named 63 explicitly -- proceeding to build the general (roll-absence) predicate, which is a superset of the named 63 and does not regress anything the dispatch asked for.

step1b_successorQuestion.countingRule: READ-ONLY, live, production. Two independent checks, both against 48055.
step1b_successorQuestion.crosswalkCheck: cad_property_vintage_crosswalk table exists (columns: county_fips, from_tax_year, from_prop_id, to_tax_year, to_prop_id, method, evidence_class, source_file, source_vintage, ingested_at) -- exactly the mechanism L21 built for named successor mapping. Queried for county_fips=48055 AND from_prop_id IN (all 267 roll-dropouts): 0 rows. No recorded successor for any of the 267, including the 63.
step1b_successorQuestion.geometryCheck: txgio_parcel carries real geometry (PostGIS geom column) keyed by prop_id, independent of cad_property's tax_year. Of the 63, two (prop_id '0' and '1') are NOT single parcels -- txgio_parcel holds 227 and 203 distinct features respectively under those ids, i.e. bucket/sentinel ids, not individually identifiable accounts (the dispatch's own worked example, 48055:1, is one of these two -- its 'account' identity is not well-formed and its reported 7.025 acres does not match the currently-served old-shape payload's own acreage of 195.2147, computed by shoelace off whichever feature the join happened to pick first). Restricting to the 47 of 63 that are genuine single-feature parcels: ST_Intersects against every prop_id present in the 2026 roll found candidate touches for 42 of 47, but ST_Area(ST_Intersection(...)) was 0 for every single one of the 157 intersecting pairs -- every 'intersection' is boundary/edge adjacency (neighboring parcels), never real polygon-area overlap. Zero of 47 single-feature retired parcels have ANY current-roll parcel whose polygon actually covers their footprint.
step1b_successorQuestion.verdict: No successor account is identifiable by either method. This is evidence AGAINST a simple renumber-into-an-adjacent-account explanation, but is not proof of deletion -- a true successor could exist on a plat not yet geometrically ingested. Per the mission's explicit instruction, NOT naming a successor: no 'superseded by' field is being built. Reporting this as an established negative, not a guess.

decision: Mechanism established from source + live data, not assumed. Proceeding to step 2 (declared retirement leaf, gated on roll-absence per fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll's declared-vintage map -- the general predicate, superset of the 63 the dispatch named), step 3 (no deletion), step 4 (propose walk grading rule). Flagging the 63-vs-267 scope correction and the successor-negative finding in the close for the operator/integration seat to weigh.
